question: Which man of the Bible am I?
reference: Matthew 3; Luke 1 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'John No. 1')

clues: My birth to elderly parents was announced by an angel, and my father was struck silent until he named me.
I wore camel's hair and a leather belt and ate locusts and wild honey in the wilderness.
I baptized people in the Jordan River and told them to repent, for the Kingdom had drawn near.
I was beheaded in prison after a girl's dance pleased Herod Antipas.

question: Which early Christian am I?
reference: Acts 4:36; 9:27; 13-15 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Barnabas')

clues: I was a Levite from the island of Cyprus, and the apostles gave me a name meaning Son of Comfort.
I sold a field and laid the money at the apostles' feet.
I vouched for the former persecutor Saul when the disciples were still afraid of him.
I later parted ways with Paul in a sharp dispute over whether to take John Mark along again.

question: Which companion of Paul am I?
reference: Acts 16:1-3; 1 Timothy; 2 Timothy 1:5 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Timothy')

clues: My mother was Eunice and my grandmother Lois, both women of faith; my father was a Greek.
I came from Lystra, and Paul had me circumcised before taking me on the road.
Paul called me his beloved and faithful child in the Lord and sent me to strengthen the congregations.
Paul urged me to stop drinking only water and take a little wine for my stomach.

question: Which teacher in the early congregation am I?
reference: Acts 18:24-28; 1 Corinthians 3:6 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Apollos')

clues: I was a Jew from Alexandria, an eloquent man well versed in the Scriptures.
At first I knew only the baptism of John.
Priscilla and Aquila took me aside and explained the way of God more accurately to me.
Paul said he planted and I watered, but God made it grow.

question: Which Roman official am I?
reference: Matthew 27; John 18-19 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Pilate, Pontius')

clues: I was the Roman governor of Judea when Jesus was brought to trial.
I said more than once that I found no crime in the man.
I offered the crowd a choice between Jesus and a prisoner named Barabbas, and washed my hands before them.
I had a sign fastened to the cross reading, The King of the Jews, and refused to change it.

question: Which ruler am I?
reference: Mark 6:14-29; Luke 23:7-12 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Herod No. 3')

clues: I was a district ruler over Galilee and Perea, and a son of Herod the Great.
I took my brother's wife, Herodias, and John the Baptist condemned me for it.
I had John imprisoned and then beheaded after a rash oath at my birthday feast.
Pilate sent Jesus to me during the trial, and I mocked him and sent him back.

question: Which follower of Jesus am I?
reference: Mark 15:43-46; John 19:38 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Joseph No. 8')

clues: I was a rich man and a respected member of the Jewish high court.
I had not agreed with the court's action against Jesus.
I was a disciple, but secretly, out of fear.
I asked Pilate for Jesus' body and laid it in my own new tomb cut in the rock.

question: Which woman of the Bible am I?
reference: Luke 10:38-42; John 11 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Martha')

clues: I lived in Bethany with my sister and brother, and I often opened my home to Jesus.
I once complained that my sister left me to do all the serving while she sat and listened.
When my brother died I told Jesus that if he had been there, it would not have happened.
I then confessed that I believed he was the Christ, the Son of God.

question: Which friend of Jesus am I?
reference: John 11; 12:9-11 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Lazarus No. 2', p. 225)

clues: I lived in Bethany with my two sisters, and Jesus loved our family.
When I fell sick my sisters sent word, but Jesus did not come until I had died.
By the time he reached my tomb I had been dead four days.
He called me by name to come out, and I walked out still wrapped in the burial cloths.

question: Which Israelite am I?
reference: Numbers 13-14; Joshua 14 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Caleb No. 1')

clues: I was one of the twelve men sent to spy out the land of Canaan.
Ten of us brought back a fearful report, but I urged the people to go up and take the land.
God said I had followed him fully, so I alone of my generation, with one other, would enter.
At 85 I asked for the hill country of Hebron and drove out the giant Anakim.

question: Which warrior of Israel am I?
reference: 1 Samuel 14; 18-20; 31 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Jonathan No. 3')

clues: I was the crown prince, the eldest son of the first king of Israel.
With only my armor-bearer I climbed up and struck down a Philistine outpost.
My soul became bound up with the young man my father came to hate, and I gave him my robe and sword.
I died beside my father and brothers on Mount Gilboa.

question: Which king am I?
reference: 1 Kings 12; 14:25-28 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Rehoboam')

clues: I inherited the throne of a very rich and famous father.
I rejected the older men's advice and told the people I would make their yoke heavier.
Ten tribes rebelled at my words, leaving me only Judah and Benjamin.
In my fifth year Shishak of Egypt came up and stripped the temple of its gold.

question: Which king of Israel am I?
reference: 2 Kings 9-10 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Jehu No. 1')

clues: A young prophet sent by Elisha poured oil on my head and anointed me king while I sat with the army officers.
I drove my chariot furiously, and a watchman said the driving looked like mine.
I had a wicked queen thrown down from her window, and dogs ate her body as the prophecy said.
I wiped out the house of Ahab and the worshippers of Baal, but kept the golden calves.

question: Which leader of the return from exile am I?
reference: Ezra 7-10; Nehemiah 8 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1, 'Ezra No. 1')

clues: I was a priest and a skilled copyist in the Law of Moses.
I came up from Babylon in the seventh year of King Artaxerxes, with the king's backing.
I had set my heart to study God's law, to apply it, and to teach it in Israel.
I read the Law aloud from daybreak to midday while all the people stood and listened.

question: Which place am I?
reference: Revelation 1:9 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Patmos')

clues: I am a small, rocky island in the Aegean Sea, off the coast of the Roman province of Asia.
The apostle John was sent here for speaking about God and bearing witness to Jesus.
While he was here on the Lord's day, a loud voice like a trumpet spoke to him.
The visions he received here became the last book of the Bible.

question: Which city of the Bible am I?
reference: Genesis 12:6-7; Joshua 24; Judges 9 (cross-check: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 2, 'Shechem No. 2')

clues: I lie in the hill country of Ephraim, in a pass between two mountains.
Abraham built his first altar in the land near my big tree, and Jacob later dug a well close by.
Joshua gathered all Israel here to renew the covenant and set up a great stone under a tree.
Abimelech destroyed me and scattered salt over my ruins; later Rehoboam came here to be made king.
